entry.title: Microtubules in mouse oocytes
entry.content:
The microtubules in oocytes of primordial follicles likely contribute to the rotation of the oocyte nucleus (1). These microtubules likely emanate from MTOCs or centrioles (2).

In oocytes of primary follicles, the microtubules are elongated and robust (2). The deposition of MTOC proteins, such as Aurora A and PLK1, contributes to this.

In oocytes of secondary follicles, the microtubules grow further and likely interact extensively with cortical actin (3).

In oocytes of antral follicles, the microtubules become short. Do they have a role in MARDO (2, 4)?
